articles.title: Before Its Reboot, the Greatest Sci-Fi Conspiracy Series of All Time Has Been Beamed Up to #1 on Streaming
articles.summary: Courtesy of 20th Century Studio When it comes to iconic TV shows, they don't come much bigger or more successful than a 90s sci-fi series that asked us to believe that the truth was out there, aliens were among us, and anything that could not be explained by science belonged in one filing cabinet deep in the bowels of the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When it comes to iconic TV shows, they don't come much bigger or more successful than a 90s sci-fi series that asked us to believe that the truth was out there, aliens were among us, and anything that could not be explained by science belonged in one filing cabinet deep in the bowels of the FBI's headquarters. You really don't need to be Mulder or Scully to know that the show we are talking about is The X-Files , which is about to return to screens with brand new creepy cases and plenty of new faces in Ryan Coogler's reboot . Before that, though, long-time fans of the series have sent the original show to the top of the Apple Store chart while they wait for confirmation whether new rumors of a possible return of Fox Mulder and Dana Scully could be on the cards have any weight to them.

It is now 33 years since the doors were open on the conspiracy-filled world of the FBI's most maligned department, The X-Files . Across nine original seasons, two movies, and a two-season revival, David Duchovny's Mulder and Gillian Anderson's Scully chased aliens, shadowy government agents, aliens posing as shadowy government agents, and other things like werewolves, poltergeists, trolls…but mostly aliens. Alongside this hunt for extraterrestrial life, the pair's relationship also gave fans one of the longest running will-they-won't-they partnerships in TV history. The series balanced its humor with some truly terrifying moments of horror that kept ratings high and cemented The X-Files its place in TV history. Despite being three decades old, the show still stands up and delivers the same chilling cases as it did when it debuted. Now, the show could be headed for a revival as well as a reboot.

It has been a few years since Ryan Coogler was said to be working on a reboot of The X-Files but in the last few months the new take has finally started picking up pace with Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel set to lead the series for Hulu. The pilot episode has already been filmed but with the show now "in the writers room," it will probably be late in 2027 or 2028 before we finally get to see what Coogler can cook up after his runaway success with movies like Black Panther and the multi Oscar-winning Sinners . There have been many opinions shared online about the reboot of the show before anyone has seen even a publicity shot, with some already writing it off as not being able to live up to its predecessor and others interested to see what Coogler can do with the property. Yet, those who feel that The X-Files is not The X-Files without its original duo may unexpectedly get to see them back on screen in a competing series.

In a recent interview, original show creator Chris Carter revealed that he already knows what comes next for Mulder and Scully and he would love to be able to pick up the story again. The revival of the series in 2016 and 2018 ended with plenty of answers, but new ambiguities for those who always believe there is another conspiracy out there to be solved. In addition to this, Duchovny told an audience at a GQ Q&A session that there were "plans" being discussed and Carter wants to "end with the original show." Meanwhile, he also noted that Coogler has spoken to him about being involved in his new series in some way. All of this is still very much up in the air right now, but what is clear is that one way or the other, The X-Files is returning with at least one new show, yet the sci-fi masterpiece's position in the Apple Store right now proves there is plenty of interest in what came before as well.

Should Mulder and Scully return, or should Ryan Coogler start with a clean slate? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: The Wildest Fantasy Movie of the 2000s Changed the Story Completely, But It Still Holds Up 19 Years Later
articles.summary: The fantasy genre in the 2000s was dominated by two franchises, as both Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings brought the world of Tolkien to life on a grand canvas and Harry Potter began to capture the imagination of the globe. Naturally, the success of both led to imitators across the decade, all of […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The fantasy genre in the 2000s was dominated by two franchises , as both Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings brought the world of Tolkien to life on a grand canvas and Harry Potter began to capture the imagination of the globe. Naturally, the success of both led to imitators across the decade , all of which gave fantasy a resurgence that it hadn't seen…arguably ever. Mainstream appeal of the fantasy genre at the time painted it as something for families and kids, but the decade had one film that fit the bill and had more in common with Heavy Metal magazine than a story about Hogwarts.

Beowulf may not be the oldest story in the world, but that it still survives is something of a miracle. Like The Odyssey before it, though, this tale of a daring Scandinavian hero who fights monsters and saves kings has been the basis for countless interpretations (including movies) over the years. When Robert Zemeckis turned it into a film that was released in 2007, though, released 19 years ago this week on November 16 , it was just the latest in a long line of takes on the material. This version of Beowulf didn't look like any other adaptation, though, and it made even wilder changes to the story itself.

In the 2000s, filmmaker Robert Zemeckis got stuck in a pretty specific niche, making motion capture movies that put layers of animation on top of live-action performances. Though the uncanny valley of The Polar Express remains the most spoken-about element of this trio of films, the ambitious storytelling ideas of Beowulf have proven to be the most interesting creative decision across them, and that's on top of distinct action and atmosphere that make it a film worth revisiting decades later.

The structure of Beowul f is pretty simple: the monster Grendel attacks King Hrothgar and his village; Beowulf eventually arrives to take down the beast, freeing the Danes from the torment of the monster; and years later a dragon attacks after Beowulf has become the king himself, with the titular hero dying to save his people one last time. Every version tells a variation of this story, but Robert Zemeckis' take brings some twists to the material.

A mid-point twist in Zemeckis' Beowulf reveals that King Hrothgar (Anthony Hopkins) was previously seduced by Grendel's mother (Angelina Jolie), not only implying that the only reason he became king was because of his deal with the "devil" but that their relationship resulted in the birth of Grendel, the monster that plagued his house. This reveal is built on top of the other big surprise, where Beowulf (Ray Winstone) falls prey to the same seduction and makes a deal with Grendel's mother to secure his own future as King.

The changes to the story don't even end there, though, as the big final act, which has traditionally just been about Beowulf confronting the dragon in his old age, brings further layers to the twist. Not only is it confirmed that Beowulf has no offspring of his own following his… rendezvous with Grendel's Mother, but the dragon is actually the result of that same tryst. It brings depth to the conflict, delivering a generational repetition of the failure of leaders and how the temptation of power creates literal monsters. Even the finale of the film shows the same thing, with Wiglaf, Beowulf's best friend, facing Grendel's mother after his death and trying to resist her temptation. Again, all invented for the film, and standing in stark contrast to basically every other interpretation.

These changes are pretty surprising for English majors who have become intimately familiar with the larger story machinations of Beowulf , but they really shouldn't be. In the script for Beowulf , written by Neil Gaiman & Roger Avary, the changes carry an implication that all the monsters were actually born from decisions by other characters like Hrothgar and Beowulf, adding depth to a fantasy tale that previously felt a little shallow in its monster-fighting mythos.

At the time of release, the changes to Beowulf 's larger story were somewhat controversial, seen as change for the sake of change, but the reality is that it gave the story something far more interesting. By flipping the machismo of Beowulf the character, and the subtext of the story, into a narrative that reveals the fallout of masculine-forward thinking and how the infrastructure of leadership can be built on a crumbling foundation built on lies. Beowulf has more than monsters; it adds meat to its bones.

There's one problem with Beowulf, and it's not the story changes; it's the look. Even though the film has a clear improvement over the animation style found in The Polar Express , there's a stiltedness to how it looks, almost like an aged Warcraft cinematic from Blizzard. To new audiences, this may be an insurmountable summit to get over in order to enjoy everything else that it has to offer.

Underneath the dead eyes and the fake skin that is found, though, Beowulf offers a rich take on an aged story and offers distinct filmmaking sensibilities that are staged impeccably. Robert Zemeckis is an Academy Award-winning director, and even though the films he's best known for aren't ones with massive action scenes and throw downs with monsters, Beowulf proved that he knew how to make it work on the big screen. It's been almost twenty years since this version came out, which is nothing compared to the lifetime of Beowulf as a story.

Actors have become increasingly vocal in recent months about their struggles amid the slowdown in production of film and television shows, drawing attention to performers’ hardships in qualifying for their union health plan and even paying their dues.

Facing pressure and online criticism to do something more for floundering members, on Friday the actors’ union SAG-AFTRA announced that its national board had voted unanimously to create a public policy-focused task force to advocate for universal healthcare. “This Taskforce seeks a new level of participation in the national movement to expand care for everyone,” Astin added. “We will actively engage with policymakers, gather allies and provide a structured way for our members to participate formally in the process. It’s a step, though far from a quick-fix solution to the problems that members have grown louder about in recent weeks. According to the latest terms the union negotiated with studios and streamers earlier this year, aimed at addressing healthcare inflation, eligibility premiums and the earnings threshold for health insurance will rise slightly in 2027, with more increases coming in the years after.

Some members have also recently faulted the labor group for dropping its COVID-era policy of keeping performers who were behind on their dues in the union. As of Nov. 1, SAG-AFTRA returned to terminating the memberships of actors who owed dues and, according to Variety , thousands have been dropped from the labor group as a result.

As these concerns were developing, its national board extended union staff leader Duncan Crabtree-Ireland ’s contract until 2032 on Oct. 24 and reportedly gave him a 15 percent raise, drawing some further scrutiny. The union explained at the time, “The extended term provides for added stability and continuity for the union during a time of unprecedented industry disruption.” But some members found the timing insensitive.

Once seen as a progressive pipe dream, universal healthcare may be becoming more politically palatable after a midterm election that hinged on affordability concerns and amid rampant healthcare inflation. But achieving it would, to say the least, be politically complex and require immense support from many quarters. Still, at a time of major healthcare challenges across the country, the union can at least point to its advocacy as a form of action.

articles.title: Days of Future Past's Most Tragic Hero Just Got a Second Chance, and It Could Have Huge Marvel Implications
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics There have been some terrible X-Men timelines where mutants ended up as victims of a society that hates them, but none are quite as bad as "Days of Future Past." This was the first major alternate timeline the mutants of Earth-616 faced, and that is because one of the mutants from that dystopian future timeline, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There have been some terrible X-Men timelines where mutants ended up as victims of a society that hates them, but none are quite as bad as "Days of Future Past." This was the first major alternate timeline the mutants of Earth-616 faced, and that is because one of the mutants from that dystopian future timeline, Kate Pryde, was sent back in time to see if she could help change the future. The sad thing is that, in Marvel Comics, when the future is changed, it only saves the timeline that stopped the terrible events from occurring, which is always Earth-616 since that is the main timeline. The other timeline, with all its horrific offerings, remains alive as an Earth in the multiverse.

X-Men Incursions #1 (2026) by Alex Paknadel and Jim Towe takes us back to Earth-811, the Earth of "Days of Future Past," and it shows that, even though Kate Pryde traveled back in time to save Earth-616 from this future, she still lives in a nightmare dystopia. It even shows that her life didn't get better and was much worse than it was before.

Of all the mutants on Earth-811, the one who was the most tragic was Kate Pryde. That is because she is the one who survived. The original "Days of Future Past" storyline was a two-issue tale that took place in The Uncanny X-Men #141-142 by Chris Claremont and John Byrne. The cover to the first issue showed the horror, as several major mutants were listed as slain, including Cyclops, Nightcrawler, Angel, Iceman, Beast, and more. This story opened with Kate Pryde alone, walking the destroyed streets of New York City. Once the youngest member of the X-Men, she is now a tired, war-weary mutant trying to stay alive.

Wolverine was still alive, albeit much older, and the story showed that Kate was working for the Sentinels to stay alive, and she passed a huge series of graves that also included the names of non-mutant heroes like Ben Grimm. They had a plan, though, as a mysterious mutant named Rachel had the powers to send Kate's mind back in time to her younger body in the past. While it wasn't revealed until later, this was Rachel Summers, the daughter of Cyclops and Jean Grey.

Kate had to return to the past to convince the X-Men to stop Mystique and the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants from killing Senator Robert Kelly, which is the event that kick-started this apocalyptic future. They succeeded, and it saved the world. But, as I mentioned, it kept the "Days of Future Past" timeline intact, as changing the past only splits the timeline and adds another Earth to the multiverse. Kate saw Wolverine and Colossus both die in the original story, and when Rachel raced through time to the past, Kate was left almost alone.

In X-Men Incursions , Kate Pryde is still fighting Sentinels, this time with her close friend Carol Danvers. However, an accident while phasing left Carol stuck halfway in the paved ground. Doctor Strange then showed up with the Black Priests to destroy Earth-811 when an incursion began with the "House of M" Earth. He showed Kate that she was a teacher on the "House of M" Earth. He also showed her that Wolverine and Nightcrawler were still alive and that Captain Marvel was one of that world's most important heroes. He revealed all this to explain why her Earth, an apocalyptic nightmare, needed to die to allow the other to survive.

However, there was a huge twist at the end of this issue. Doctor Strange and the Black Priests destroyed Earth-811 to save the "House of M" Earth, believing that destroying bad Earths to save good ones could somehow stop the incursions from continuing. Before he could destroy the world, Kate asked him to save something, to save anything. Doctor Strange agreed in the end and did something unexpected. Right as the "Days of Future Past" world was destroyed, he sent Kate Pryde to a different Earth, where she was left unconscious in a field that Colossus was working in.

This was astonishing, and it raises a lot of questions about where Marvel is going with this. Doctor Strange not only saved Kate Pryde from her Earth as he destroyed it, but also sent her to another Earth, one that looks much more peaceful than the one she left. Remember, in the original storyline, she was married to Colossus, and she lost him. Now, she is on an Earth without Sentinels raining terror on her, and she is reunited with Colossus. The big thing to note is that this moves Kate to a different Earth, and while every Earth was destroyed in "Time Runs Out," the re-creation of the multiverse after "Secret Wars" could open the door for a new storyline, and Kate Pryde could be a huge part of that, dealing with her loss and her new future. In the end, it could change everything we know about the original incursions.

What are your thoughts on X-Men Incursions and its implications for the original "Time Runs Out" storyline? Let us know where you think this is all heading in the comments below.

articles.title: A Panned Marvel Movie with a 15% RT Score Is Crawling into the Streaming Charts 2 Years After Derailing an Entire Franchise
articles.summary: Courtesy of Sony Pictures If you think the Marvel Cinematic Universe has had a tough time keeping audiences entertained over the last several years, that is nothing compared to another branch of Marvel cinema that has failed time and time again to make movies that people care about despite being linked to one of the most profitable and popular […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If you think the Marvel Cinematic Universe has had a tough time keeping audiences entertained over the last several years, that is nothing compared to another branch of Marvel cinema that has failed time and time again to make movies that people care about despite being linked to one of the most profitable and popular superheroes of all time. Yet, even a run of movies that everyone seems to hate and completely collapsed during their cinema run can have their day on streaming, which is exactly why two years after its disastrous debut, Madame Web is finding a new audience as it ascends the HBO Max global movie chart. For a movie that was exterminated by critics, memed to death on social media, and even had its star failing to give much in the way of positive press for it, the resurrection of Sony's MCU adjacent film is something almost as illogical as most of Madame Web 's plot.

Released in February 2024 - a month renowned for producing box office disappointment - Madame Web was released as the latest in Sony's Spider-Man Universe franchise that previously included such cinematic masterpieces as Morbius … they wish. Other than Tom Hardy's Venom trilogy, the movies released in this disjointed, connected-not-connected project did not hold much interest for audiences, resulting in plenty of box office losses. Madame Web did not manage to change their fortunes, but instead only succeeded tolling the bell for the end of the chaotic run of movies set in a Spider-Man universe without Spider-Man. When it debuted, Madame Web struggled to get out of single figures with its Rotten Tomatoes score, and even now the critics rating sits on a terrible 15% approval score, and that set it on a path to a $100.5 million total worldwide gross. Yet, even as one of the biggest bombs of the century, there are always people willing to give it a click on streaming.

On paper, just like all of Sony's Spider-Man Universe movies, the film should have at least been able to provide the studio with a moderate hit. The film gathered together an ensemble of high-profile female stars led by Dakota Johnson as Cassandra "Cassie" Webb , a New York paramedic who discovers she has the ability to see into the future. Her power seems to be directing her to save three other women, played by Sydney Sweeney, Isabela Merced, and Celeste O'Connor, from a Spider-Man-esque killer called Ezekiel (Tahar Rahim). Many of the actors, Sweeney in particular, were making small ripples in Hollywood, so should have been able to pique interest. Instead, the film's take-it-or-leave-it plot combined with heavily criticized cliché-ridden dialogue, turned most people off from seeing it in cinemas.

That did not stop the film topping the Netflix chart when it was released on the platform just a few months later, as watching as part of a subscription is very different to paying to see it. In the last two years, most of the cast have gone on to better things, with Johnson, Sweeney and Merced's profiles in particular expanding greatly. Whether this is now part of the reason many who skipped the movie the first time around are giving it a go on HBO Max is hard to tell, but a low-commitment half-watch at home is where this movie seems to have found its audience. With this particular arm of Marvel movies now seemingly dead, with Kraven the Hunter being the final nail in the coffin , Madame Web 's streaming success really isn't going to change the fate of the franchise. Instead, it just suggests that Spider-Man centric characters just aren't that special without a web-slinger appearing alongside them.

articles.title: Someone Made Obsession Look Like A Disney Channel Movie, And Why Does This Fit SO Well?
articles.summary: I did not see this crossover coming.
articles.content:
A good measure of how popular and beloved a movie is these days is how often the internet memeifies it, and Obsession is oozing with viral tributes. From all those Nikki memes to that gross cat scene becoming a popular Halloween costume, the horror movie is clearly one of the most memorable 2026 movies . I just found a new video that really took Obsession to a whole new level for me.

No, no, no, don’t do that! I would never have believed you if you told me I’d be saying Obsession and Disney Channel in the same sentence, but here I am. Honestly, this is so impressive. It really does transform one of the scariest scenes in the whole movie into a more lighthearted comedy thanks to the soundtrack, laugh tracks and graphics that famously play on Disney Channel. Check out some of the comments:

My favorite part of the video has to be when Nikki does her iconic backwards walk back into the corner and there’s a laugh track. I mean, like the comments say, it really is crazy how important the sound can transform a scene because I sort of believe the scene in this wild universe where it’s a Disney Channel film – minus the muted colors and two characters sharing the same bed.

Now, if you recall the Backrooms ending , what happens next is a lot darker, but it’s still funny to see the same scene redone to try to fit the Disney Channel aesthetic. These movies are two of the most popular horror films of the year, so this crossover is the ultimate way to change how we typically think of them.

articles.title: Matt Damon Went Viral For A Cute Disneyland Video, But The Story Behind It Is Even Lovelier
articles.summary: Time slows for no one, not even a celebrity dad.
articles.content:
Matt Damon was clearly trying to fly under the radar during an August 2026 trip to Disneyland to celebrate his daughter Gia’s 18 th birthday. Then he ended up clearly visible in the background of internet comedian and content creator Loryn Powell’s video on Instagram, as her daughter was meeting Goofy for the first time. And the video of the movie star dad smiling as he watched and understood how special the father-daughter moment in front of him was unsurprisingly went vital.

When I first saw the video, I immediately thought, “Now there’s a dad who’s having a flashback of a memory with his own daughter.” So it warmed my heart to hear directly from the Good Will Hunting star that that’s exactly what happened. He, himself, has had that exact moment over the year on annual birthday trips that landed him in that very same spot.

I love when the timing lines up and someone can ask a celebrity to explain the story behind a viral moment, making them more relatable to everyone else. And there’s nothing more human than spending and missing time with our loved ones. I can’t imagine what the family in the video thought when they realized that not only was The Bourne Identity star at Disneyland on the same day, but he was in the background of their video, reacting to that special interaction.

articles.summary: A PS2 series is now available on PS5 and PS4 for $2.24, courtesy of the new PlayStation Store sale. More specifically, a 2001 PS2 game and its 2002 PS2 sequel are both now available for PS5 and PS4 users at this price. That said, the deal that makes this price point possible is set to […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A PS2 series is now available on PS5 and PS4 for $2.49, courtesy of the new PlayStation Store sale. More specifically, a 2001 PS2 game and its 2002 PS2 sequel are both now available for PS5 and PS4 users at this price. That said, the deal that makes this price point possible is set to expire on the morning of November 21, in about eight hours from the moment of publishing. And unlike many PS2 games on the PlayStation Store, these aren't included with a PS Plus Premium subscription, so right now the only way to play them on PlayStation is to buy them.

Back in 2001 and 2002, developer Volition — the studio that would go on to create Saints Row and the studio that no longer exists as of 2023 — combined with publisher THQ to release Red Faction and Red Faction 2 . Both games ended up being multi-platform, but were notably PS2 exclusives at launch. In the second half of the 2010s, the pair of sci-fi first-person shooters were re-released on the PlayStation Store with new features like trophy support and widescreen resolutions, but they are still the original PS2 versions of the games.

In 2009, a third game was released, Red Faction: Guerrilla , but the original version of this game doesn't exist on the PlayStation Store; only the 2018 remaster which costs $30 and isn't on sale. Then there was a fourth game in 2011, Red Faction: Armageddon , which is also the final game in the series, and it's not available on the PlayStation Store in any capacity.

Two Great PS2 First-Person Shooters The first Red Faction game received an 88 on Metacritic and was notably one of the best games of its year, hence why it spawned a four-game franchise, complete with a spin-off as well. The sequel wasn't received quite as well, but it still earned a very solid score of 84.

Do the pair of first-person shooters hold up? Yeah, they do, especially the first game. The first game stood out back in the early 2000s for its proprietary Geo-Mod destruction system that gave the game destructible environments and open-ended gameplay long before these things became common. And for a PS2 first-person shooter, its gunplay still holds up pretty well. By comparison, Red Faction II is a far more traditional and linear first-person shooter from this era. It has less uniqueness, but overall it still feels viable to play in 2026. If you don't have nostalgia for this era of gaming, though, it could be difficult to travel two decades back in time and experience these in their dated glory.

For those who end up checking out the pair of PS2 games, the first game is about 6 to 9 hours long, while the second is about 4 to 6 hours long. This may seem short, but it was standard for first-person shooter campaigns at the time. Meanwhile, if this PlayStation Store sale doesn't tickle your fancy, there is currently another great PS2 first-person shooter series available at the same price on the digital Sony storefront .

articles.title: Macy’s Bringing Back Its Blue Hippo For The 100th Parade, And Fiona The Hippo Fans Have A Request
articles.summary: A blue hippo is making its way back this Thanksgiving
articles.content:
The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is hitting a significant milestone this year and will be turning the big 100. To celebrate, they are pulling out all the stops, including adding favorites, both new and old. One returning balloon has fans emotional as the announcement comes after the tragic death of Fiona the Hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden. Now that Macy’s has brought back its blue hippo for the 100th parade, Fiona fans have a request.

In addition to the balloon possibly representing Fiona, it also has a long, legendary history. It was first unveiled in 1931, and during that parade, they decided it was a good idea to release giant balloons into New York City. You may be asking yourself, why? I’ll tell you. Each balloon had a price tag, and whoever found a balloon and returned it to the department store would receive that amount as a prize. The blue hippo balloon was never returned, and even after an offer of $100, nobody came forward, leaving the balloon lost to history.

If the blue hippo isn’t enough to sell you on the parade, then maybe some new floats might. We’ll be seeing a variety of newcomers, including "Hogwarts Holiday," which features a Harry Potter -themed float that will celebrate (and promote) the newly rebooted series on HBO kicking off in December. The cool floats and balloons are an opportunity for brands (like Starbucks) to promote themselves with whimsical, colorful, and unique floats or balloons.

articles.title: Godzilla x Kong: Supernova Could Introduce A Dangerous Kaiju That Already Destroyed Godzilla Before

Over the years, our big reptilian giant has more than held his […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Over the course of his existence, Godzilla , the King of the Monsters, has fought an infinite variety of enemies. There's no shortage of battles, from titanic monsters to ancient enemies, from metallic monstrosities to things that make a disaster in Tokyo look insignificant. Over the years, our big reptilian giant has more than held his own and always managed to come out on top. But what do you do when another foe comes along who can match his fury and even use his strength against him? That's a major problem.

The upcoming film, Godzilla x Kong: Supernova , could hold an answer that's as entertaining as it is terrifying. Rumors about the film suggest we could be getting a new killer from the depths of space and onto the big screen to stand toe-to-toe with Godzilla. This is not a simple titanic creature you'd like to see in a backyard bash. No, this one is cosmic and very much connected to Godzilla's very DNA.

There's the possibility of SpaceGodzilla, a terrifying cosmic opponent. Making his debut in the 1994 flick Godzilla vs. SpaceGodzilla , this alien menace is a nightmare version of Gojira. Or… well, his backstory makes very little sense. Godzilla's cells were carried into space, reportedly by either Biollante or Mothra, before being exposed to intense cosmic radiation near a black hole. The resulting mutation eventually produced SpaceGodzilla, an extraterrestrial monster with Godzilla's genetic makeup and extraordinary crystalline powers. The result was a creature with Godzilla's DNA and an entirely different arsenal. SpaceGodzilla isn't just a duplicate. He has powers that create a brand-new set of problems.

In this trailer, you can see SpaceGodzilla put in the work with his incredible powers. Everything about this is fantastic nostalgia mixed with the history and heritage of the Japanese franchise. If you're a newer Godzilla fan, you definitely need to check out the classic movies.

And those gnarly-looking giant crystals attached to his shoulders serve a purpose besides looking intimidating. SpaceGodzilla has the ability to control the crystals, levitate objects, fire powerful energy blasts, and create a photon shield to deflect Godzilla's powerful atomic breath attack. While it is true that Godzilla's atomic breath is not as effective against the photon shield, the fact that he can do this in the first place is a huge advantage. On top of all that, the monster is able to draw power from his environment to get even more powerful.

The first confrontation between these two scaly goliaths was nothing short of epic. When Godzilla vs. SpaceGodzilla began, the alien foe had the edge. During their first confrontation on Birth Island, SpaceGodzilla easily overpowered Godzilla before trapping Little Godzilla inside a crystalline prison. The alien monster then traveled to Fukuoka, where he constructed an enormous crystal fortress and began drawing energy from the Earth's core. Godzilla needed M.O.G.U.E.R.A.'s help to take down this alien titan. In order to be victorious, the King of the Monsters needed to destroy the enemy's crystal towers and cut off the energy that made the beast so powerful.

Fans have started to tie this mysterious kaiju to Godzilla x Kong: Supernova for a very compelling reason. One rumor cited a Writers Guild of America directory that seemingly listed SpaceGodzilla among the source characters for the movie. That's not confirmation by any means, but it does keep curious fans wondering. Should he turn up in the MonsterVerse, he'll bring with him an entirely different form of threat. Whereas Godzilla and Kong have faced seemingly hundreds of titanic foes over the years, a cosmic monster with the ability to form his own energy fortress would take things to an entirely new level. We may be getting ready for the strangest Godzilla battle we've ever seen in the MonsterVerse . And honestly, we're pretty sure that would be a good thing.

You know, Godzilla has faced plenty of monsters in his city-stomping career, but fighting an evil cosmic version of himself is actually a whole new level of family drama. After all, nobody knows how to push your buttons quite like someone with your DNA! Talk about annoying sibling twins…. Would you like to see SpaceGodzilla become the next big MonsterVerse villain? Tell us your dream matchup in the comments!

articles.title: Supernatural Star Confirms Sequel Series Ideas, And It Would Change a 15 Season Formula
articles.summary: It’s been six years since Supernatural ended its legendary 15 season, 327 episode run and concluded the story of Dean and Sam Winchester, but that doesn’t mean that fans have ever quite let go of the story. There was a one-season spin-off, comic books, and people still wonder if we’ll ever get a sequel of […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It’s been six years since Supernatural ended its legendary 15 season, 327 episode run and concluded the story of Dean and Sam Winchester, but that doesn’t mean that fans have ever quite let go of the story. There was a one-season spin-off, comic books, and people still wonder if we’ll ever get a sequel of some sort. As it turns out, series star Jared Padalecki has a few ideas about that, but it would see a major change to the iconic series’ formula and would look a lot more like another iconic series, Gilmore Girls .

Speaking with Collider , Padalecki revealed that not only does he have an idea for what a follow-up to Supernatural would look like in terms than story, but the format it would take. Padalecki says that instead of a long, 20-episode season it would be more like four, 90-minute ones in the vein of how Gilmore Girls returned in 2016 and as for the story? Well, Sam and Dean would end up back on Earth with no idea how or why.

“They’ve got work to do,” Padalecki said. “They don’t know exactly what yet. They don’t know why they’re even there, but they have to sleuth it out.”

While there is without a doubt fan desire for more Supernatural and especially more of Sam and Dean — the series’ finale was widely divisiv e among fans, particularly in terms of Dean’s death and the characters that were absent in the overall story, a Gilmore Girls’ revival style follow up might not be the answer. Padalecki’s rationale is understandable as the schedule to make 4 longer episodes over a full 20-episode season is a better fit for his family, but when Gilmore Girls: A Year In the Life debuted in 2016, many fans felt like the format messed with the show’s pacing, giving the story a lot more “filler” than it would have otherwise had. There were also concerns that the structure didn’t serve the characters well, leaving things uneven and somewhat unsatisfying.

Given the way fans feel about Supernatural ’s existing finale and what would no doubt be sky-high expectations for any sequel or follow up, a four-part follow up feels like a bit of a risk. That said, it would also likely come down largely to the actual details of the story itself. The idea of Sam and Dean coming back to Earth for some mysterious purpose offers up a lot of space for interesting storytelling as well as rich character returns. If done correctly, the pacing issues that Gilmore Girls faced might not even be a problem. The only thing that we know for sure is something that Padalecki himself is also very clear on: if they did do a follow up to Supernatural , it couldn’t be a prequel.

“The one thing we cannot do is a prequel because we look a lot older than we did 25 years ago, or 21 years ago,” Padalecki said.

Would you want a Gilmore Girls -style Supernatural follow up? Hit us up in the comments and the forum to sound off.
